Baseline for this program is TIGER_BEHAVIOR_RQ-VAE (test_R@10 = 0.061927).
That arm fed the contrastive term from ``pair_cycle = cycle(pair_loader)``
built once before the epoch loop. ``itertools.cycle`` materialises its first
pass and replays it forever, so the sampler's ``set_epoch`` was a no-op, only
``ceil(339519 / 512) = 664`` distinct pair batches per rank were ever drawn, and
the ~36,000 draws of the active epochs wrapped that frozen pool about 54 times
with an identical negative pool every time.

This tree fixes that and adds one optional mechanism, selected by hardcoded
constants so each arm's committed state is exactly what ran:

  RESAMPLE_PAIRS      rebuild the pair iterator every epoch (True for both arms;
                      an arm with this False is the baseline's behaviour)
  FALSE_NEGATIVE_MASK drop candidates that are themselves known successors of
                      the anchor, not just repeats of the anchor's own target.
                      The baseline masked only duplicate targets, so a second
                      real successor was still pushed away as a negative.
  EXPERIMENT_ARM      "resample" or "resample_fn_mask"; drives the output paths

Everything else is unchanged: ``model/`` stays byte-identical to TIGER, and the
3000-epoch budget, deduplicated item batch, AdamW warmup + linear decay,
codebook sizes, KMeans init and seed 42 all stay as the baseline fixes them.
The delayed ramp stays as the baseline's: 0 at epoch 1500, 0.2 at epoch 3000.

"""TIGER + iter48 behaviour contrastive with corrected pair sampling.

Baseline for this program is TIGER_BEHAVIOR_RQ-VAE (test_R@10 = 0.061927).
That arm fed the contrastive term from ``pair_cycle = cycle(pair_loader)``
built once before the epoch loop. ``itertools.cycle`` materialises its first
pass and replays it forever, so the sampler's ``set_epoch`` was a no-op, only
``ceil(339519 / 512) = 664`` distinct pair batches per rank were ever drawn, and
the ~36,000 draws of the active epochs wrapped that frozen pool about 54 times
with an identical negative pool every time.

This tree fixes that and adds one optional mechanism, selected by hardcoded
constants so each arm's committed state is exactly what ran:

  RESAMPLE_PAIRS      rebuild the pair iterator every epoch (True for both arms;
                      an arm with this False is the baseline's behaviour)
  FALSE_NEGATIVE_MASK drop candidates that are themselves known successors of
                      the anchor, not just repeats of the anchor's own target.
                      The baseline masked only duplicate targets, so a second
                      real successor was still pushed away as a negative.
  EXPERIMENT_ARM      "resample" or "resample_fn_mask"; drives the output paths

Everything else is unchanged: ``model/`` stays byte-identical to TIGER, and the
3000-epoch budget, deduplicated item batch, AdamW warmup + linear decay,
codebook sizes, KMeans init and seed 42 all stay as the baseline fixes them.
The delayed ramp stays as the baseline's: 0 at epoch 1500, 0.2 at epoch 3000.

+    """Compute the proposal's directed assignment and endpoint-separation loss."""
+    temperature = float(parameters.get("temperature", 0.2))
+    margin = float(parameters.get("margin", 0.05))
+    min_separation = float(parameters.get("min_separation", 0.2))
+    separation_weight = float(parameters.get("separation_weight", 1.0))
+    eps = float(parameters.get("eps", 1e-8))
+    weight = float(parameters.get("weight", 0.005))
+

+    p = torch.softmax(-torch.cdist(source, codebook).square() / temperature, dim=-1)
+    q = torch.softmax(-torch.cdist(target, codebook).square() / temperature, dim=-1)

+    code_delta = codebook.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0) - codebook.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(2)
+    projection = torch.einsum("bijd,bd->bij", code_delta, direction) / (direction_norm.squeeze(-1)[:, None, None] + eps)

Implemented the directed assignment-repartition mechanism in `mechanism_directed_capacity_preserving_assignment_repartition.py` and wired it into `train_rqvae.py`.

The term uses separate soft assignments for source and target, a directional codeword-pair cost, and an expected endpoint-separation penalty. It uses the level-0 residuals and codebook, with the proposal’s hardcoded weight and parameters. It is computed inside the `epoch_weight > 0.0` region and added to the host loss before backward, so its gradients can flow through the encoder and codebook via the normal optimizer path.

`py_compile` passed for both files. I couldn’t run the numeric or gradient checks because PyTorch is unavailable in this environment.

"""TIGER + iter48 behaviour contrastive with corrected pair sampling.

Baseline for this program is TIGER_BEHAVIOR_RQ-VAE (test_R@10 = 0.061927).
That arm fed the contrastive term from ``pair_cycle = cycle(pair_loader)``
built once before the epoch loop. ``itertools.cycle`` materialises its first
pass and replays it forever, so the sampler's ``set_epoch`` was a no-op, only
``ceil(339519 / 512) = 664`` distinct pair batches per rank were ever drawn, and
the ~36,000 draws of the active epochs wrapped that frozen pool about 54 times
with an identical negative pool every time.

This tree fixes that and adds one optional mechanism, selected by hardcoded
constants so each arm's committed state is exactly what ran:

  RESAMPLE_PAIRS      rebuild the pair iterator every epoch (True for both arms;
                      an arm with this False is the baseline's behaviour)
  FALSE_NEGATIVE_MASK drop candidates that are themselves known successors of
                      the anchor, not just repeats of the anchor's own target.
                      The baseline masked only duplicate targets, so a second
                      real successor was still pushed away as a negative.
  EXPERIMENT_ARM      "resample" or "resample_fn_mask"; drives the output paths

Everything else is unchanged: ``model/`` stays byte-identical to TIGER, and the
3000-epoch budget, deduplicated item batch, AdamW warmup + linear decay,
codebook sizes, KMeans init and seed 42 all stay as the baseline fixes them.
The delayed ramp stays as the baseline's: 0 at epoch 1500, 0.2 at epoch 3000.

+"""Directed soft-assignment repartition regularizer for transition pairs."""
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+
+def mechanism_loss(source, target, codebook, mask, **parameters):
+    """Compute the proposal's directed assignment and endpoint-separation loss."""
+    temperature = float(parameters.get("temperature", 0.2))
+    margin = float(parameters.get("margin", 0.05))
+    min_separation = float(parameters.get("min_separation", 0.2))
+    separation_weight = float(parameters.get("separation_weight", 1.0))
+    eps = float(parameters.get("eps", 1e-8))
+    weight = float(parameters.get("weight", 0.005))
+
+    # Soft assignments are independently formed from each directed endpoint.
+    p = torch.softmax(-torch.cdist(source, codebook).square() / temperature, dim=-1)
+    q = torch.softmax(-torch.cdist(target, codebook).square() / temperature, dim=-1)
+    direction = target - source
+    direction_norm = torch.linalg.vector_norm(direction, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    code_delta = codebook.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0) - codebook.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(2)
+    projection = torch.einsum("bijd,bd->bij", code_delta, direction) / (direction_norm.squeeze(-1)[:, None, None] + eps)
+    directed_cost = F.softplus((margin - projection) / temperature)
+
+    distances = torch.cdist(codebook, codebook)
+    separation_cost = F.softplus((min_separation - distances) / temperature)

I’ll inspect the training loss/ramp and existing arm conventions first, then add the standalone mechanism module and wire it into the active pair-loss branch before backward. I’ll leave the host loss, optimizer, initialization, seeds, and training budget untouched.
Implemented the directed assignment-repartition mechanism in `mechanism_directed_capacity_preserving_assignment_repartition.py` and wired it into `train_rqvae.py`.

The term uses separate soft assignments for source and target, a directional codeword-pair cost, and an expected endpoint-separation penalty. It uses the level-0 residuals and codebook, with the proposal’s hardcoded weight and parameters. It is computed inside the `epoch_weight > 0.0` region and added to the host loss before backward, so its gradients can flow through the encoder and codebook via the normal optimizer path.

`py_compile` passed for both files. I couldn’t run the numeric or gradient checks because PyTorch is unavailable in this environment.

+"""Directed soft-assignment repartition regularizer for transition pairs."""
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+
+def mechanism_loss(source, target, codebook, mask, **parameters):
+    """Compute the proposal's directed assignment and endpoint-separation loss."""
+    temperature = float(parameters.get("temperature", 0.2))
+    margin = float(parameters.get("margin", 0.05))
+    min_separation = float(parameters.get("min_separation", 0.2))
+    separation_weight = float(parameters.get("separation_weight", 1.0))
+    eps = float(parameters.get("eps", 1e-8))
+    weight = float(parameters.get("weight", 0.005))
+
+    # Soft assignments are independently formed from each directed endpoint.
+    p = torch.softmax(-torch.cdist(source, codebook).square() / temperature, dim=-1)
+    q = torch.softmax(-torch.cdist(target, codebook).square() / temperature, dim=-1)
+    direction = target - source
+    direction_norm = torch.linalg.vector_norm(direction, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    code_delta = codebook.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0) - codebook.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(2)
+    projection = torch.einsum("bijd,bd->bij", code_delta, direction) / (direction_norm.squeeze(-1)[:, None, None] + eps)
+    directed_cost = F.softplus((margin - projection) / temperature)
+
+    distances = torch.cdist(codebook, codebook)
+    separation_cost = F.softplus((min_separation - distances) / temperature)
+    expected = (p.unsqueeze(2) * q.unsqueeze(1) *
+                (directed_cost + separation_weight * separation_cost.unsqueeze(0))).sum(dim=(1, 2))
+    valid = mask.to(device=expected.device, dtype=expected.dtype)
+    return weight * (expected * valid).sum() / valid.sum().clamp_min(1.0)
